Done — the product title now renders instantly as part of a prerendered static shell, while the live inventory streams in.

The problem was in `app/product/page.tsx`: the whole page `await`ed `getInventory()`, which calls `connection()` and forces per-request rendering, so navigation from home blocked on the inventory fetch before anything appeared.

The fix, following this version's Cache Components docs (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/06-fetching-data.md`): the page component is now synchronous and renders the "Premium Widget" title immediately, and the dynamic data moved into a nested async `<Inventory>` component wrapped in `<Suspense>` with a "Checking availability…" fallback. Stock count and price stream in when `getInventory()` resolves.

Verified with `next build`: `/product` now shows as `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — static HTML shell with dynamic server-streamed content — so the prefetched title paints on navigation with no build errors. (The build also auto-adjusted `tsconfig.json`, a standard Next.js side effect.)
